attack_technique: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
description: Adversaries may cause a DoS by exhausting resources on an endpoint service. Slowloris is a specific 'low-and-slow' tool that achieves this by opening multiple connections to the targeted web server and keeping them open as long as possible. It does this by continuously sending partial HTTP requests, holding server threads open indefinitely and preventing legitimate users from connecting.

patterns.description: The defining signature of Slowloris involving the deliberate manipulation of HTTP header completion.

features.name: Incomplete HTTP Headers (Missing CRLF)
features.description: The client sends a valid HTTP request line and headers but intentionally withholds the final blank line (Carriage Return Line Feed - CRLF / '\r\n\r\n') required to terminate the header block. The server waits indefinitely for the request to finish.

features.name: Bogus Header Drip-Feeding
features.description: To prevent the server from timing out the idle connection, the client periodically sends fake, randomized, or redundant HTTP headers (e.g., 'X-a: b') at extremely slow intervals.

patterns.description: Anomalies in how long connections are held open and the pacing of the packets.

features.name: Extreme Connection Longevity
features.description: The overall lifespan of a single network flow (High Flow Duration) is artificially extended for minutes or hours, successfully bypassing short-term session timeouts.

features.name: Prolonged Inter-Arrival Times
features.description: Massive deliberate delays exist between the packets sent by the client (High Flow IAT Mean and High Fwd IAT Max). The attacker waits until just before the server's timeout threshold to send the next partial header.

patterns.description: Anomalies indicating a deliberate lack of bandwidth utilization to exhaust server threads instead of network pipes.

features.name: Thread Starvation (Non-Volumetric)
features.description: The attack uses minimal network bandwidth (Low Flow Pkts/s) but aims to tie up all available worker threads or processes on the target server (famously effective against thread-based servers like older Apache versions).

features.name: Micro-Packet Sizing
features.description: The average size of the packets being sent (Low Packet Length Mean) is tiny, as the attacker is only sending a few bytes of text (a single header line) every few seconds or minutes.

patterns.description: Contextual indicators for distinguishing the attack from poor network conditions.

features.name: DDoS Appliance Evasion
features.description: Because the TCP three-way handshake is completed legitimately and the bandwidth footprint is negligible, volumetric DDoS protection appliances often fail to detect Slowloris.

features.name: Congested Network Resemblance (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: Clients on extremely slow, congested networks, or devices with severe packet loss, may naturally exhibit behaviors similar to low-and-slow partial request attacks.
